challenge.reason: The old decision's own rationale (fewer than 20 issues per run, single-file simplicity) no longer holds: runs now admit 200+ issues and the concurrency executor writes many issues in parallel. Per-issue files address the two concrete failures named (lock contention on one file, one corrupt byte losing the whole run) and keep the same directory root with an index for discovery. The supersession argument is sound. Residual risk for the build, not the decision: index and per-issue files can disagree after a partial write, so index updates need to be atomic or rebuildable from the directory.
